format.name: agent-journal/events-jsonl
format.record_rule: a line whose top-level member 'declaration' is an object is a declaration record; every other line is an OCSF execution event carrying class_uid
format.upstream_validation: the pinned upstream OCSF validator is run on execution records only (every line without a top-level 'declaration' member); declaration records are validated by the reader against declaration_definitions
format.lifecycle: declarations are append-only and written before the first event that references them; a 'recording' declaration marks finalization (COMPLETED or INTERRUPTED); a file without one is an open prefix, or the writer failed, which only the ancillary run.json can state
format.ancillary: run.json beside this file is an index and summary (final hash, counts, failure detail, extension source, semantic contract, mapping audit); it is not needed to interpret this file and may be absent

extension.name: agentic_cli
extension.reader_rule: resolve class names through this table; refuse a file whose pinned uid/class table differs from the reader's compiled schema

time_policy.time: source-reported time when the record has one (time_basis 1); else the latest preceding reported time in the same artifact, else capture start (time_basis 2); metadata.original_time holds the source text verbatim; ordering is journal.sequence, never time
time_policy.severity_id: always 0 Unknown: Journal convention, not a vendor assertion

schema.definition_policy: each class, object and scalar type is declared before the first event that uses it: extension-defined classes and objects complete; core objects with their required attributes plus those the events use, amended by a later definition record when an event uses a further attribute; profile-only attributes of profiles the events do not enable omitted

launch_settings.command: replay of the sanitized live stream (original: <path> -p Use the MCP server named journal_echo. 1. Call its tool echo_record with arguments {"text": "alpha", "n": 1}. 2. Do not use any other tool and do not run shell commands. Finally reply in one line with the two echo values returned and whether always_fails reported an error. --output-format stream-json --verbose ...)

system/thinking_tokens.limit: observed on every tested route (2.1.299 sdk, 2.1.303 sdk, 2.1.304 stdout); its relation to the reported final thinking_tokens is not specified by the vendor and is not asserted here

system/task_lifecycle.meaning: system/task_started, task_updated, and task_progress or task_notification without a usage object: sub-agent task lifecycle notifications (task_id, the spawning tool_use_id, subagent_type, description, prompt, status)

mcp.target: a tool_use whose full name is a tool the init record lists, and that exactly one server the init record registers (mcp_servers[].name) makes mcp__<server>__<tool> with a non-empty tool, is an MCP call: target_server_name and target_tool_name are a declared derivation (basis 3 Declared derivation from an encoded tool name), target_arguments_pointer is the empty pointer (the input is the tool's own arguments); an ambiguous or unregistered name has no target; tool_name and arguments stay as reported
mcp.projections: the request projects CallToolRequestParams {arguments: tool_use.input} (name missing: the server-side name is the derived target, not a reported member); the result projects CallToolResult {structuredContent: tool_use_result.structuredContent} when reported (content missing: the stream's result content is a rendering, not MCP content blocks)
mcp.errors: a tool_result with is_error true of an MCP call is tool_result.errors layer 3 CLI-reported tool failure with the result text as its message; the stream does not say whether the server returned isError or a JSON-RPC error
mcp.not_reported: the negotiated protocol revision, JSON-RPC ids, isError, capabilities and the MCP content blocks of a result
mcp.binding: ocsf/mcp/binding.json 0.1.0 (generated by McpBindingGenerator from schema/protocol/mcp/PINS.json); every projection is a partial projection typed by the 2025-11-25 binding because this route does not report the negotiated protocol revision; the projected members are defined identically in both pinned revisions

1.caption: Canonical single observation
1.description: The only observation of its entity and stage among the declared sources.

2.caption: Supporting observation
2.description: One source's observation of an entity whose consolidated canonical event is in the same file.

3.caption: Consolidated canonical
3.description: The canonical event of an entity and stage that several sources observed, built from their compatible fields with per-field evidence.

2.caption: Representation only
2.description: Equal values spelled differently (1 and 1.0).

3.caption: One richer
3.description: One observation carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

4.caption: Each richer
4.description: Each carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

5.caption: Conflicting
5.description: Two observations report different values for one field.

6.caption: Ambiguous
6.description: The identity repeats within one source, so no pairing is established.

7.caption: Single source
7.description: Only one observation reports the field.

8.caption: Superseded
8.description: A provisional observation of a quantity that a final observation of the same quantity (same scope, aggregation and model) supersedes: the canonical event carries the final one and the provisional one stays on its supporting observation, never counted again.

1.caption: Full reasoning
1.description: The model's reasoning text as produced.

2.caption: Summary
2.description: A summary of the model's reasoning, not its full text.

3.caption: Redacted
3.description: The source reports that reasoning occurred but withholds its text (for example encrypted or redacted reasoning).

1.caption: Increment
1.description: The text continues the item's text: the item's text is the concatenation, in journal.sequence order, of the texts of its Increment blocks. An increment is not by itself asserted to be the whole text, and the assembled text is never concatenated with a whole text reported elsewhere (for example a turn's own response).

2.caption: Snapshot
2.description: The text is the item's whole text as of this record: it replaces any earlier view of the item and is never concatenated with one.

1.caption: Monetary amount
1.description: Money in the stated currency.

2.caption: Premium requests
2.description: A count of premium requests the CLI reports as consumed.

3.caption: Model cost multiplier
3.description: A per-call model multiplier, or a sum of such multipliers, that a vendor reports for billing; not money and not a request count.

4.caption: Nano-AIU
4.description: Nano AI units a vendor reports.

1.caption: Scope total
1.description: The consumption of exactly the observation's scope unit (for example one model response); observations of distinct units of that scope are disjoint.

2.caption: Cumulative snapshot
2.description: A running total of the scope unit from its start up to the point of observation. It may include consumption before this capture began and is not the unit's completed total; two snapshots of one unit overlap and are never summed.

7.caption: Child run
7.description: The run of a sub-agent that a tool call spawned. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation); its observations are never added to the parent's or the run's totals.

It is not established to be the unit of any other scope (a conversation step is not stated to be one model response), and units of different source artifacts are never joined by equal identifiers. 1.description: Copied exactly from the one native member named.

2.caption: Derived
2.description: Computed exactly from the native members named, by the declared rule in derivation, whose arithmetic the source establishes.

3.caption: Unavailable
3.description: The source reports related members, but they do not establish this component (derivation states why); the component is absent, never zero.

1.caption: Measured
1.description: The source establishes this exact value as a measurement of the quantity; for a running total, of every contribution to it.

2.caption: Possibly default
2.description: The source emits exactly these values also when it has no measurement (for example all-zero defaults); a measured value is not established.

3.caption: Conditional
3.description: On a usage component whose canonical value the source does not establish: a declared formula gives a result from the reported operands that is the component's quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (for example that a possibly default operand, or one that is only a lower bound, is a complete measurement). The result is the component's conditional_value, never the canonical value, which stays absent. A price estimate from it holds only under the same assumptions. Equal prices for the tranches between which the uncertain quantity could fall make that allocation immaterial to their subtotal; they do not make the subtotal exact when an operand is itself a lower bound, because no price recovers a contribution the source never reported.

4.caption: Lower bound
4.description: The quantity is at least this value, and that it equals the quantity is not established: the value sums measured contributions while a contribution the source did not receive, or for which it wrote its default, is missing (for example a running total that adds only the responses whose usage arrived and writes 0 for an omitted member). A positive running total therefore does not establish that every contribution was reported: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150. The value is kept as reported, never raised to a guessed quantity, and a price estimate computed from it is itself only a lower bound of the charge.

progressToken.description: If specified, the caller is requesting out-of-band progress notifications for this request (as represented by notifications/progress). The value of this parameter is an opaque token that will be attached to any subsequent notifications. The receiver is not obligated to provide these notifications.

arguments.description: Arguments to use for the tool call.

task.description:
If specified, the caller is requesting task-augmented execution for this request.
The request will return a CreateTaskResult immediately, and the actual result can be
retrieved later via tasks/result.

Task augmentation is subject to capability negotiation - receivers MUST declare support
for task augmentation of specific request types in their capabilities.

ProgressToken.description: A progress token, used to associate progress notifications with the original request.

Metadata for augmenting a request with task execution.
Include this in the `task` field of the request parameters.

ttl.description: Requested duration in milliseconds to retain task from creation.

conventions.object: a JSON Schema object with properties is an OCSF object mcp_<snake(definition)> (inline: mcp_<owner>__<member>); every protocol member is an optional OCSF attribute and the protocol's required list stays here
conventions.member_attribute: an object-typed member is held in an attribute named after its type (_list for an array or a map); a scalar or free-JSON member in mcp_<snake(member)>, suffixed with its signature when that member name has more than one signature in the pinned revisions
conventions.variant: a union is a variant object with one attribute per alternative and mcp_unresolved for a value that no single alternative matches by its JSON type, constant members and required members (ties keep the alternatives with more matched constants, then more matched required members, then fewer unnamed members)
conventions.map: a map whose values have a schema is an array of entry objects: mcp_key plus the typed value, in source order
conventions.json: free JSON (JSONValue, JSONObject, an empty or open object without properties, arrays of free JSON) and scalar unions are json_t, preserved exactly
conventions.preservation: mcp_additional_members keeps members a definition does not name; mcp_nonconforming_members keeps named members whose value does not fit; nothing is dropped
conventions.requirement: OCSF requirement is optional for every generated attribute so that partial CLI projections validate; complete objects are validated against the pinned JSON Schema, and a projection lists the required members it lacks

Annotations.description: Optional annotations for the client. The client can use annotations to inform how objects are used or displayed

audience.description:
Describes who the intended audience of this object or data is.

It can include multiple entries to indicate content useful for multiple audiences (e.g., `["user", "assistant"]`).

lastModified.description:
The moment the resource was last modified, as an ISO 8601 formatted string.

Should be an ISO 8601 formatted string (e.g., "2025-01-12T15:00:58Z").

Examples: last activity timestamp in an open file, timestamp when the resource
was attached, etc.

priority.description:
Describes how important this data is for operating the server.

A value of 1 means "most important," and indicates that the data is
effectively required, while 0 means "least important," and indicates that
the data is entirely optional.

_meta.description: See [General fields: `_meta`](/specification/2025-11-25/basic/index#meta) for notes on `_meta` usage.

content.description: A list of content objects that represent the unstructured result of the tool call.

isError.description:
Whether the tool call ended in an error.

If not set, this is assumed to be false (the call was successful).

Any errors that originate from the tool SHOULD be reported inside the result
object, with `isError` set to true, _not_ as an MCP protocol-level error
response. Otherwise, the LLM would not be able to see that an error occurred
and self-correct.

However, any errors in _finding_ the tool, an error indicating that the
server does not support tool calls, or any other exceptional conditions,
should be reported as an MCP error response.

structuredContent.description: An optional JSON object that represents the structured result of the tool call.

EmbeddedResource.description:
The contents of a resource, embedded into a prompt or tool call result.

It is up to the client how best to render embedded resources for the benefit
of the LLM and/or the user.

Icon.description: An optionally-sized icon that can be displayed in a user interface.

mimeType.description:
Optional MIME type override if the source MIME type is missing or generic.
For example: `"image/png"`, `"image/jpeg"`, or `"image/svg+xml"`.

sizes.description:
Optional array of strings that specify sizes at which the icon can be used.
Each string should be in WxH format (e.g., `"48x48"`, `"96x96"`) or `"any"` for scalable formats like SVG.

If not provided, the client should assume that the icon can be used at any size.

src.description:
A standard URI pointing to an icon resource. May be an HTTP/HTTPS URL or a
`data:` URI with Base64-encoded image data.

Consumers SHOULD takes steps to ensure URLs serving icons are from the
same domain as the client/server or a trusted domain.

Consumers SHOULD take appropriate precautions when consuming SVGs as they can contain
executable JavaScript.

theme.description:
Optional specifier for the theme this icon is designed for. `light` indicates
the icon is designed to be used with a light background, and `dark` indicates
the icon is designed to be used with a dark background.

If not provided, the client should assume the icon can be used with any theme.

ImageContent.description: An image provided to or from an LLM.

_meta.description: See [General fields: `_meta`](/specification/2025-11-25/basic/index#meta) for notes on `_meta` usage.

mimeType.description: The MIME type of the image. Different providers may support different image types.

ResourceLink.description:
A resource that the server is capable of reading, included in a prompt or tool call result.

Note: resource links returned by tools are not guaranteed to appear in the results of `resources/list` requests.

_meta.description: See [General fields: `_meta`](/specification/2025-11-25/basic/index#meta) for notes on `_meta` usage.

description.description:
A description of what this resource represents.

This can be used by clients to improve the LLM's understanding of available resources. It can be thought of like a "hint" to the model.

icons.description:
Optional set of sized icons that the client can display in a user interface.

Clients that support rendering icons MUST support at least the following MIME types:
- `image/png` - PNG images (safe, universal compatibility)
- `image/jpeg` (and `image/jpg`) - JPEG images (safe, universal compatibility)

Clients that support rendering icons SHOULD also support:
- `image/svg+xml` - SVG images (scalable but requires security precautions)
- `image/webp` - WebP images (modern, efficient format)

mimeType.description: The MIME type of this resource, if known.

name.description: Intended for programmatic or logical use, but used as a display name in past specs or fallback (if title isn't present).

size.description:
The size of the raw resource content, in bytes (i.e., before base64 encoding or any tokenization), if known.

This can be used by Hosts to display file sizes and estimate context window usage.

title.description:
Intended for UI and end-user contexts — optimized to be human-readable and easily understood,
even by those unfamiliar with domain-specific terminology.

If not provided, the name should be used for display (except for Tool,
where `annotations.title` should be given precedence over using `name`,
if present).
